profile.name: Erza Duraku
profile.tagline: I build software with logic, curiosity, and a little bit of creativity—focused on software development, AI, and full-stack engineering.
profile.intro: Software Engineering student at the University of Pristina, interested in software development, AI, backend systems, cloud computing, DevOps, and full-stack engineering.

projects.title: Predictive Text Engine
projects.oneLiner: A text prediction system exploring algorithms, language patterns, and efficient suggestions.
projects.summary: A problem-solving project focused on turning data structures and prediction logic into a practical interaction.
projects.problem: The goal was to predict likely next words and provide autocomplete while handling different n-gram approaches and text filtering.
projects.whatIBuilt: Worked with bigram and trigram models, the Brown corpus, profanity filtering, and Trie-based autocomplete. The project evolved from a Java/JavaFX version into a Python/Tkinter implementation.
projects.learned: How language can be represented computationally, how different n-gram approaches behave, and how data structures such as Tries can support fast autocomplete.

projects.title: HR Contracts / Payroll
projects.oneLiner: A structured system for managing employee contracts and payroll-related information.
projects.summary: Built around reliable data modeling, clear workflows, and the practical needs of administrative software.
projects.problem: The system needed to represent employees, contracts, payroll-related information, permissions, and relationships across a larger relational model.
projects.whatIBuilt: Worked with the database structure, relationships, SQL, and role-based access concepts across an 18-table PostgreSQL design.
projects.learned: How to model a larger relational system, think about relationships between entities, and keep data access structured and controlled.

projects.title: AWS TicketHub
projects.oneLiner: A cloud-focused ticketing project built while learning modern infrastructure workflows.
projects.summary: Connected application development with deployment, automation, and infrastructure concepts.
projects.problem: The project explored how a backend can be structured using managed cloud services instead of maintaining a traditional server.
projects.whatIBuilt: Worked with the core serverless architecture and service integration.
projects.learned: How cloud services can be combined into a backend system, and how serverless architecture changes the way application components communicate.

projects.title: CollabAI
projects.oneLiner: A full-stack, AI-powered project management platform for organizing teams, projects and tasks, with a built-in AI assistant that uses RAG and semantic search over the organization’s data.

projects.title: DCADD Master Project
projects.oneLiner: Terraform infrastructure on AWS for a highly available web application: a multi-AZ VPC, private EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling Group behind an Application Load Balancer, deployed with GitHub Actions.

projects.title: Text Rule Processor
projects.oneLiner: A rule-based content filter web app: users define rules that detect patterns in text and mark them with highlights or tooltips, with a history of processed text.

projects.title: Maze Solver Visualizer
projects.oneLiner: An interactive maze editor and pathfinding visualizer that uses A* search with a Manhattan-distance heuristic to find the shortest path.

projects.title: Group 1 Master Web App
projects.oneLiner: The static web page for the DCADD Master Project (Group 1), served from private EC2 instances behind the load balancer.

projects.title: Firebase Auth
projects.oneLiner: Firebase Authentication project using Email/Password and Google Sign-In.

experience.summary: My first professional engineering environment—contributing to real product development, translating requirements and designs into functional interfaces, and learning to work carefully inside an existing codebase.
experience.comparison: University projects taught me how to build something from the beginning. Working professionally taught me how to build inside something that already exists. That difference changed how I think about software.
learningPoints: Working inside an existing codebase rather than starting everything from zero.
Understanding how requirements and designs translate into implementation.
Collaborating with other people and communicating about technical work.
Using Git and development workflows in a professional environment.
Thinking about maintainability and how a feature fits into the larger product.
Connecting frontend work with backend systems and real product requirements.

volunteering.title: SFK 2025 — 10th Edition
volunteering.short: I helped with event coordination, workshop setup, participant guidance, and speaker support—experiencing the open-source community from the inside.
body: SFK 2025 was one of my first opportunities to become actively involved in the local technology and open-source community. Instead of experiencing the event only as a participant, I joined the volunteer team and became part of the work happening behind the scenes.
During the event, I helped with workshop setup, guided participants, supported speakers, and assisted with the overall coordination of activities.

volunteering.title: Digi Camp & Digital Skills Festival
volunteering.short: For three days in May, I volunteered at Digi Camp & Digital Skills Festival at ITP Prizren, helping the workshops, sessions, and festival activities run smoothly. I was glad to be part of it, and even more glad that I got to explore ITP itself.
body: From 21 to 23 May 2026, ITP Prizren hosted Digi Camp & Digital Skills Festival, a three-day, international-level technology festival. I joined as a volunteer, and most of my time went into helping organize and run the workshops, sessions, and festival activities, along with the operational tasks that keep an event like this moving.
I collaborated with professionals and mentors throughout, and being close to their work taught me a lot about how a festival like this actually comes together.

I was also very glad I got to explore ITP. The Innovation & Training Park Prizren is a hub for entrepreneurship, innovation, and skills, built on the former KFOR camp site, and it connects companies, start-ups, and universities with a focus on ICT and the creative industries. Spending three days there showed me what it looks like when a place is built for people to learn and create.

volunteeringQuote.quote: I came to these events to help. I left each one having learned something.
volunteeringQuote.reflection: Volunteering has given me experiences that I could not get from university projects alone. It taught me how to communicate with different people, work as part of a team, adapt when plans change, and take responsibility for making things work.

about.heading: Somewhere between two worlds, I found software engineering.
about.lead: I am, in many ways, a product of two very different kinds of work.
paragraphs: My father is a mechanic; my mother is a tailor. One world of engines and tools, the other of fabrics and patterns. From my father I learned the value of showing up, being patient, and finishing what you start—the kind of work ethic that comes from fixing things carefully, not rushing past the hard parts.

From my mother I inherited a different kind of attention: creativity, and the habit of noticing small details. Growing up around sewing, patterns, measurements, and handmade work taught me that creating something takes both an idea and the patience to turn that idea into something real.

Somewhere between those two sides, I found software. I enjoy understanding how things work, breaking complex problems into smaller pieces, and building solutions that make sense. I care about how something works, but also how it feels, looks, and comes together as a whole—because building well, for me, has always meant both logic and care.
about.quote: "I don't know yet" is not a weakness. It is the beginning of figuring it out.
about.beyondLead: These interests may seem unrelated to software, but they all share something: patience, curiosity, and the satisfaction of creating or understanding something.

purpose.label: Where I want to go
purpose.heading: Something I care about beyond code.
paragraphs: I grew up close to a child with Down syndrome, and I saw what daily life can look like for a family like theirs. In Kosovo, the right support is hard to find, and many families are left to figure it out alone.

I study software engineering, and I love it. Someday I want to work with organizations that support children with autism, Down syndrome, and other special needs, building tools that save teachers time, apps families can actually use, and interfaces that feel calm. I am still at the beginning.
I want to build things well, for people who are too often forgotten.
